subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: Should OpenClaw expose inbound sender identity as a configured principal or stable provider ID, expose a raw trusted display-name field, or keep display names untrusted until a broader authorship contract lands?
rationale: This changes which identity facts agents may treat as authoritative for private-message routing and session context, and the safest authority source is a product/security decision rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Approve Configured Principal
options.body: Expose only an operator-configured canonical principal or stable provider-id-derived identity in trusted metadata, keeping human display names in untrusted context.

options.title: Expose Raw Display Name
options.body: Add sender_display_name as trusted metadata, accepting higher spoofing, privacy, and cache-stability review burden.

options.title: Defer To Authorship Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader chat.send authorship and shared-session identity model settles the common contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Configured Principal
recommendation.body: Expose only an operator-configured canonical principal or stable provider-id-derived identity in trusted metadata, keeping human display names in untrusted context.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits on the trusted/untrusted prompt metadata boundary where this owner has the strongest current history signal.
